scope_note: Initial fresh-programme literature inventory. Source quality and scope are explicit; no source implies internal reproduction.

sources.citation: Mu, X. (2007). Weather, storage, and natural gas price dynamics: fundamentals and volatility. Energy Economics 29(1), 46-63.

replication_contract.market_source: Commodity Research Bureau (formerly Bridge) daily natural-gas futures trading data
replication_contract.project_fidelity_boundary: canonical Databento history starts in 2010, so source-period exact replication is impossible; source-method near replication is required
replication_contract.return_semantics: daily log changes of settlement prices; two series from nearest and second-nearest contracts
replication_contract.roll_rule: RET1 replaces the nearest-contract return on the contract's final trading day with the same-day second-nearest return to avoid thin-market expiry distortion
replication_contract.samuelson_tests: RET1 unconditional variance exceeds RET2 by one-sided F-test at 1%; separate GARCH(1,1) conditional variances are compared, with h1_t reported above h2_t in 954 of 998 paired cases

sources.citation: Brown, S.P.A. and Yucel, M.K. (2008). What Drives Natural Gas Prices? The Energy Journal 29(2), 45-60.

replication_contract.lag_semantics: VAR lag order 5, corresponding to 4 lagged first differences in the VECM
replication_contract.method: Johansen cointegration rank test and VECM/error-correction representation
replication_contract.project_source_route: Roberts (2019) public revisit/replication package provides the prepared Brown-Yucel dataset and exact Stata command sequence for source-period reproduction
replication_contract.source_result: one long-run Henry Hub/WTI relationship in the source period; natural-gas price adjusts to disequilibrium while oil is weakly exogenous; weather, storage and hurricane controls strengthen the relationship

sources.citation: Roberts, G. (2019). Revisiting the Drivers of Natural Gas Prices. International Journal for Re-Views in Empirical Economics.

replication_contract.source_result: Brown-Yucel long-run oil-gas relationship is reproduced in the 1997-2007 sample and disappears in the full and post-2007 samples

replication_data.repository: International Journal for Re-Views in Empirical Economics data archive

sources.citation: Geman, H. and Ohana, S. (2009). Forward curves, scarcity and price volatility in oil and natural gas markets. Energy Economics 31(4), 576-585.

replication_contract.gas_inventory_sample: U.S. natural-gas stocks at each month end, 1992-12-31 through 2006-07-31, from EIA/DOE
replication_contract.gas_market_sample: daily NYMEX monthly natural-gas futures, January 1993 through August 2006, maturities 1 through 13 months
replication_contract.inventory_alignment: one-month-lagged deseasonalized inventory is primary; source states contemporaneous inventory gives the same qualitative conclusions
replication_contract.inventory_deseasonalization: OLS on constant + cos(2*pi*t/12) + sin(2*pi*t/12) + cos(2*pi*t/6); residual is deseasonalized inventory
replication_contract.monthly_volatility: annualized standard deviation of returns of the front-month futures price over consecutive trading days within each month
replication_contract.primary_test: Spearman rank correlation under one-sided negative-correlation alternative, separately for whole sample and scarcity periods, using original and deseasonalized front-month volatility
replication_contract.project_fidelity_boundary: The pinned EIA NG bulk identifies the source inventory family as NG.N5020US2.M (U.S. Total Natural Gas in Underground Storage (Working Gas), Monthly): fitting the paper's exact 1992-12 through 2006-07 trigonometric specification yields coefficient magnitudes 2.1053, 0.6390, 0.6283 and 0.1699 Tcf versus published 2.11, 0.63, 0.64 and 0.17. The same pinned bulk contains official NYMEX Contract 1 daily prices (NG.RNGC1.D) from 1994-01-13, so a source-period near replication covers 1994-01 through 2006-08 but cannot recover the paper's first approximately 12 months of 1993 market observations. Canonical Databento 2010+ is retained only as a later-regime extension. The paper does not specify arithmetic versus log daily returns or a more detailed rolling convention; arithmetic Contract-1 returns are primary, log returns fixed robustness.
replication_contract.source_result: For natural gas, inventory-volatility correlation is non-significant over the whole sample but strongly negative during scarcity; the published paper also reports that this negative relationship strengthens importantly in winter.
replication_contract.volatility_deseasonalization: OLS on constant + cos(2*pi*t/12) + cos(2*pi*t/6) + sin(2*pi*t/6); residual is deseasonalized front-month volatility

sources.citation: Gay, G.D., Simkins, B.J. and Turac, M. (2009). Analyst forecasts and price discovery in futures markets: The case of natural gas storage. Journal of Futures Markets 29(5), 451-477.
sources.data_scope: Analyst-storage-forecast database is constructed from Bloomberg surveys; reported source-study coverage is April 1997 through August 2005.

sources.citation: Mirantes, A.G., Poblacion, J. and Serna, G. (2013). The stochastic seasonal behavior of energy commodity convenience yields. Energy Economics 40, 155-166.

replication_contract.fidelity_boundary: canonical Databento begins 2010-06-04 and cannot reconstruct the full 1999-2011 source sample; the paper also does not identify the zero-coupon interest-rate data source/curve construction in the recoverable text. A Databento later-sample futures-ratio/carry reproduction must therefore keep the missing interest-rate term explicit and cannot be labeled exact convenience-yield replication.
replication_contract.market: NYMEX Henry Hub natural-gas futures; maturities available from one month to six years
replication_contract.primary_seasonality_series: contiguous F1-F9 futures prices and implicit adjacent-month convenience yields delta1-delta9
replication_contract.seasonality_test: compute calendar-month averages from each weekly series, then Kruskal-Wallis across the 12 calendar months; chi-square(11) critical value 24.725 at 99%
replication_contract.source_result: strong monthly seasonality in Henry Hub convenience yields while the futures-price series do not reject monthly no-seasonality; convenience-yield seasonality is clearer than futures-price seasonality

sources.citation: Chiou-Wei, S.-Z., Linn, S.C. and Zhu, Z. (2014). The response of U.S. natural gas futures and spot prices to storage change surprises. Journal of International Money and Finance 42, 156-173.
sources.data_scope: Uses weekly Bloomberg consensus analyst forecasts as the storage-change expectation proxy; source-study sample covers August 30, 2002 through August 18, 2011.

sources.citation: Ergen, I. and Rizvanoghlu, I. (2016). Asymmetric impacts of fundamentals on the natural gas futures volatility. Energy Economics 56, 64-74.

replication_contract.continuity_rule: Do not assume the fully specified 2010 dissertation precursor is method-identical to the final 2016 article. The final article explicitly describes TTM in days and its public estimation excerpt differs from the precursor zero-mean specification.

dissertation_precursor_2010.maturity_model: Gaussian GARCH(1,1) variance equation adds storage-report-day, Monday, December-February winter, business-days-to-maturity TTM, then TTM*WIN
dissertation_precursor_2010.return_semantics: compute log return within each individual contract first, then select the earliest-maturing active contract for each session
dissertation_precursor_2010.source_result: TTM is negative/significant before interaction; after TTM*WIN is added standalone TTM t-stat is -0.15 while the winter combined TTM effect has t-stat -8.416

replication_contract.project_fidelity_boundary: canonical Databento history begins in 2010, after the precursor source sample. Exact source-period reproduction is unavailable; the precursor method may be tested on later pre-sealed history only as a separately labeled continuity diagnostic, while the final-2016 refinement remains fidelity-bounded unless its complete final estimation contract is recovered.

published_2016.mean_equation_public_evidence: publisher text reports a long-term average return of -0.1386% and reasonable autocorrelation, then states that a first-order term is included; the publicly accessible excerpt truncates before the exact final mean equation is fully recoverable
published_2016.method_fidelity_status: final-paper maturity claim is directly recoverable, but the complete final estimation equation and exact final sample are not fully recoverable from the accessible publisher text
published_2016.published_maturity_measure: time to maturity in days included directly in the conditional variance equation
published_2016.published_maturity_result: maturity impact is seasonally asymmetric and present only during winter

replication_contract.core_finding: More than 50% of annual futures return is generated on EIA storage-announcement days; announcement-day and non-announcement-day average returns differ significantly and the announcement premium is negative.
replication_contract.intraday_secondary: Two-hour announcement return is reported as 49.4% pre-announcement and 50.6% post-announcement; a 90-minute-pre to 30-minute-post short strategy is reported at about 12% annual return, t=2.93, Sharpe 1.76 after costs.
replication_contract.market_source: Bloomberg daily price, volume and open interest for 499 Henry Hub NYMEX natural-gas futures contracts (ticker NG)
replication_contract.project_fidelity_boundary: Canonical exact listed-contract Databento history begins 2010-06-04, so the exact 2003-2018 Bloomberg sample is unavailable. Stage A is a source-method near replication on the 2010-06 through 2018-12 overlap using the source roll rule and a conservative EIA release calendar; holiday-shift weeks lacking exact historical release-day proof are excluded. Bloomberg analyst consensus is unavailable, so surprise-controlled persistence remains a separate fidelity boundary.
replication_contract.roll_rule: Szymanowska et al. (2014): roll the entire curve at the end of the month preceding the month prior to delivery
replication_contract.surprise_refinement: The paper reports the announcement-day difference survives storage-surprise and other controls; storage surprise uses analyst expectations and is not required to test the unconditional core anomaly.

sources.citation: Liang, C., Xia, Z., Lai, X. and Wang, L. (2022). Natural gas volatility prediction: Fresh evidence from extreme weather and extended GARCH-MIDAS-ES model. Energy Economics 116, 106437.
sources.scope: Source-faithful design uses EIA Henry Hub 1-month futures from January 1995 to July 2021 and historical weather variables including wind speed, temperature and precipitation; New York and Louisiana are reported weather locations. This is not evidence for issued-weather-forecast-vintage inputs. Exact weather-provider identity remains to be verified.
